title: What Strava Data Tells Us About How Runners Train for Western States (Trail Runner / Outside, Strava column, 14 Jun 2023)
population: Western States 100 finishers 2018-2022 as compiled from Strava data; finishers only, sample size not stated.
findings: Median peak week 81 miles, 16 hours and 13.5K ft of gain; 22% peaked four weeks out, 19% three weeks out, 11% five weeks out.
Median longest run 50 miles; 57% logged a long run of 50 miles or more; 43% did at least a 100K in the lead-up; 65% did at least one race in the build-up.
All finishers logged at least one 20-mile long run; on average 10 runs of 20 miles or more in the build-up; 97% logged at least a 50K, on average three 50Ks in the six months before the race.
In the peak week the median long run was 32 miles (many a self-supported or race 50K); 32% did a 50-mile race in their peak week.
Median base entering the six-month lead-up: 37 miles per week with 2,700 ft of climbing and a 12-mile long run.

The article states no statistically significant variation from other US 100-milers in peak-week timing or long-run length. Back-to-backs are not discussed apart from the Memorial Weekend Western States training runs (a 50K, 19- and 20-mile days).
limitations: Journalistic descriptive summary, not peer reviewed; finishers only so no association with finishing; races and supported training runs count as long runs; Strava self-selected sample; medians given without distributions.
implications: Real 100-mile finishers' longest runs (median 50 miles, over 9 hours for most) are far above a 240 min target and above a 6 h cap, but races and 50K-100K events dominate; a 6 h cap is stricter than observed practice and should be labelled a conservative default, grade D.
Median peak-week long run of 32 miles in an 81-mile week is roughly 40% of weekly distance (derived from two medians, approximate).
Peak week 3-4 weeks out is the modal timing, which fits a taper starting about 3 weeks before a 100 miler.
